market_summary: <cite index="30-2">A punishing sell-off rippled through Wall Street on Thursday, wiping out roughly $2.5 trillion in market value from the Nasdaq Composite on fears that Democrats' midterm gains could put the brakes on the AI buildout.

items.headline: Nvidia Plunges 9.3% on AI Stock Sell-Off and Data Center Concerns
items.summary: <cite index="5-3">NVIDIA shares fell 9.3% to $181.60 on trading volume roughly double the average, amid a broader technology and AI-stock selloff.</cite> <cite index="5-4">Investor concerns include data-center project delays and financing risks, export-control uncertainty, and high expectations ahead of NVIDIA's November 17 results.</cite>

items.headline: OCBC Q3 Net Profit Rises 3% to S$2.04 Billion, Beats Forecasts
items.summary: <cite index="10-3">Singapore's second-largest lender posted net profit of S$2.04 billion for the July to September quarter, up from S$1.98 billion a year earlier and slightly above the S$2.01 billion average estimate.</cite> <cite index="10-4">The bank now expects loan growth in the low double digits for 2026, compared with its previous forecast of high-single-digit to low-double-digit growth.</cite>

items.headline: UOB Q3 Net Profit Misses Forecasts at S$1.25 Billion
items.summary: <cite index="20-4">UOB's net profit for the third quarter came in at SG$1.25 billion, underperforming the mean estimate of SG$1.35 billion.</cite> <cite index="20-3">The Singapore lender lowered the full-year outlook for its net interest margin, as it expects funding costs will remain elevated.</cite>

items.headline: DBS Q3 Net Profit Dips 2% to S$2.95 Billion, Beats Estimates
items.summary: <cite index="19-3">DBS, Southeast Asia's biggest lender, said it expects 2026 net profit to be slightly below this year's after reporting a 2% drop in third-quarter earnings to S$2.95 billion, beating analysts' estimates of S$2.72 billion.</cite> <cite index="19-4">The DBS board declared a total dividend of 75 Singapore cents per share for the quarter, up from 54 cents a year ago.</cite>

items.headline: Apple Raises $7.5 Billion from Investment-Grade Debt Offering
items.summary: <cite index="38-1">Apple Inc. raised $7.5 billion from its high-grade bond offering, attracting solid demand from investors seeking a break from a glut of AI-related debt deals despite a broader selloff across markets.</cite> <cite index="38-3">Investors placed about $31 billion of orders on the transaction at its peak, or more than four times its size.</cite>

items.headline: Tech Giants Caught in Broad Market Sell-Off Following Midterm Elections
items.summary: <cite index="33-4">Some of the biggest names in tech took it on the chin, with Facebook parent company Meta down 3.4%, Microsoft down 2.8%, and Nvidia down 8%.</cite> <cite index="29-12">The sell-off comes amid concerns that a Democratic-controlled Congress could usher in tighter restrictions on data-center development, potentially weighing on demand for AI-related infrastructure and chips.</cite>

items.headline: Amazon Challenges Google Shopping With Direct Product Feeds
items.summary: Amazon has launched efforts to challenge Google Shopping by allowing merchants to provide direct product feeds, offering an alternative to Google's established shopping platform amid the broader tech selloff.

items.headline: Nasdaq 100 Plunges 5.5% as Tech Sector Enters Correction Territory
items.summary: <cite index="28-5">The tech-heavy Nasdaq 100 plunged 5.5% to 26,878 points by mid-morning, putting it on course for one of its biggest daily losses in recent years.</cite> <cite index="28-3">Fears of tighter regulation of artificial intelligence (AI) triggered a sell-off in US technology stocks on Thursday, two days after Democrats scored major victories in congressional elections.</cite>

items.headline: S&P 500 Falls 3.2%, Dow Drops 2.2% in Broad Market Sell-Off
items.summary: <cite index="28-6">The broader S&P 500 fell 3.2% to 7,444 points, while the blue-chip Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 2.2% to 52,193 points.</cite> <cite index="30-7">The sell-off was widespread, with all 11 sectors in the S&P 500 closing lower.</cite>
